claims.text: Separately calculating lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr will reduce prediction errors relative to previous approaches.
Prior experiments characterized defect-minimized bulk crystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
Some prior HfNbTaTiZr specimens contained approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
A rigorously calculated Debye temperature and phonon-scattering framework can predict temperature-dependent phonon transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Electronic heat transport can be independently predicted from electronic band structure and resistivity models.
The proposed model is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
Lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable near the low-temperature end of the proposed range.
Intrinsic lattice structure and local vibrational properties mediate lattice heat transport independently of delocalized electronic states.
Atomistic-simulation validation of analytical phonon calculations will refine lattice-conductivity predictions.
Separating phonon and electronic transport avoids conflation errors in earlier approaches.
Separate parameterization of phonon and electronic mechanisms improves prediction accuracy.
The model will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error by approximately 30–50% relative to prior combined methods.
The phonon contribution will be slightly dominant around 200 K.
Above 300 K, lattice and electronic contributions will be clearly separable.
Summed lattice and electronic predictions will give a high-temperature total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m).
Earlier approaches merge lattice and electronic contributions and can have errors exceeding 50%.
Oversimplified Debye temperatures and inadequate phonon-electron decoupling cause substantial uncertainty in earlier predictions.
The approach may not apply to samples with high defect concentrations or non-equilibrium microstructures.
Model performance will depend on sample purity, microstructure, and phonon and electronic parameter sensitivity.
